blindSummary: Went furthest on non-cooperation: a 2023 law declares out-of-state anti-trans law "against the public policy of this state/province" and blocks out-of-state warrants, arrests and extradition related to gender-affirming care — a state/province refusing to enforce other states'/provinces' hostility. Shield/refuge coverage places it in the strongest-protection group of the July 2026 independent legal-risk map.
blindSourceSummaries: State session law text (a 2023 chapter law, effective 28 April 2023): prevents use of state/provincial process — subpoenas, records, warrants, arrests and extradition — to assist out-of-state investigations or enforcement of laws interfering with gender-affirming health care, amends child-custody and child-welfare provisions accordingly, and declares such out-of-state laws contrary to the public policy of the state/province.

Anti-trans national legal-risk assessment map, July 2026 edition: per-state/province legal-risk grading of every state in this country; the July update added a fourth state to the map's lowest-travel grade, while classifying this state/province among the strongest-protected states (shield/refuge coverage most likely to counteract federal anti-trans rules).
blindLocalsOnly: The 2023 law's shields — subpoena, warrant and extradition bars around gender-affirming care — operate on residents, providers and families; visitors mainly read them as official posture.
